name: Indoor vertical farming
title: Vertical farming after AeroFarms and Bowery: still a no-go
question: Is indoor vertical farming viable again?
answer: AeroFarms, AppHarvest, Bowery, Plenty and Kalera raised billions and filed for bankruptcy or shut down in 2023-25. Lighting a crop indoors costs electricity the sun gives a field for free, so the model needs power to get much cheaper. US retail electricity has risen instead: the BLS city average went from about 13 cents per kWh in 2019 to about 20 cents in 2026.
verdict_reason: The killing input, electricity, got more expensive. Waiting makes it worse.

constraint.name: Electricity price versus free sunlight
constraint.detail: Indoor farms replace sunlight with LEDs; the business closes only if power costs fall far enough to beat field-grown produce.
